previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with cirrhosis from chronic hepatitis C and hepatocellular carcinoma, was admitted for observation after a planned radiofrequency ablation was canceled due to the tumor's proximity to the IVC. Instead, a liver biopsy and fiducial seed placement were performed. Post-procedure, she had a drop in hematocrit from 32 to 25, indicating a slow bleed, likely from the biopsy site. She remained hemodynamically stable, received one unit of packed red blood cells and clotting factors, and was monitored closely. Her propranolol was held initially to avoid masking tachycardia from bleeding but was restarted when stable. She was discharged home in good condition with no active bleeding, instructions to follow up on biopsy results, and no medication changes.

Brief Hospital Course:

hepatocellular carcinoma who was admitted from her PCP's office 
with persistent hyperglycemia.

secondary to infection given the acute presentation. She had a 
chest film on admission that was concerning for possible 
pneumonia, so she was treated with a 5 day course of 
levofloxacin. Urinalysis was concerning for urinary tract 
infection; however, culture was contaminated by genital flora.

tailored her insulin regimen appropriately to cover her 
hyperglycemia.

Discharge Instructions:
It was a pleasure being involved in your care, Ms. ___. You 
were admitted to the hospital with very high blood sugars.  You 
were found to have a lung infection which can be a common cause 
of high blood sugars.  Your infection was treated with 
anti-biotics and  you were given extra insulin to help keep your 
blood sugars undercontrol. 

Please make the following changes to your medications:
1. Discontinue taking your Iron (FERROUS GLUCONATE).
2. We have added Levofloxacin, please take this for three days 
after discharge.
3. Make sure you do not take your calcium pills within two hours 
of your Levofloxacin.
4. We have increased the sliding scale doses of your humalog 
insulin with meals and we have kept the lantus insulin at the 
same dose.

Please continue to take your medications as indicated.

Call your physician ___ 911 if you experience any of the 
following: crushing chest pain, difficulty breathing, 
intractable nausea or vomiting, fevers/chills, blood in your 
urine vomit or stool or any other concerning medical problem.

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  ___ female with new hyperglycemia, infectious workup.
Evaluate for pneumonia or infiltrate.

COMPARISON:  ___.

CHEST, PA AND LATERAL:  The heart is normal in size.  The mediastinal and
hilar contours are unremarkable.  There are areas of linear scarring in the
lung bases bilaterally.  However, additional patchy opacities within the left
lower lung, with bronchial wall thickening in bilateral lung bases, are
concerning for a developing bronchopneumonia. No pleural effusion or
pneumothorax is identified. There are clips in the right upper quadrant.

IMPRESSION:  Findings concerning for developing bronchopneumonia in the left
lung base.  Follow-up CXR post treatment is suggested to assess for
resolution.
